Kazakhstan is the world's [ninth-largest country by land area](/wiki/List_of_countries_and_dependencies_by_area "List of countries and dependencies by area") and the largest landlocked country. [Hilly plateaus](/wiki/Steppe "Steppe") and plains account for nearly half its vast territory, with [lowlands](/wiki/Upland_and_lowland "Upland and lowland") composing another third; its southern and eastern frontiers are composed of mountainous regions. The sky is usually clear above the desert, and the [sunshine duration](/wiki/Sunshine_duration "Sunshine duration") is extremely high everywhere in the Sahara. Most of the desert has more than 3,600 hours of bright sunshine per year (over 82% of daylight hours), and a wide area in the eastern part has over 4,000 hours of bright sunshine per year (over 91% of daylight hours). The highest values are very close to the theoretical maximum: a value of 4,300 hours, representing 98% of the total number of daylight hours per year, has been recorded both in [Upper Egypt](/wiki/Upper_Egypt "Upper Egypt") ([Aswan](/wiki/Aswan "Aswan"), [Luxor](/wiki/Luxor "Luxor")) and in the Nubian Desert ([Wadi Halfa](/wiki/Wadi_Halfa "Wadi Halfa")).[[20]](#cite_note-books.google.fr-20) The annual average direct [solar irradiation](/wiki/Solar_irradiance "Solar irradiance") is around 2,800 kWh/(m2 year) in the Great Desert. The Sahara has a huge potential for solar energy production.

Nauru had 17 changes of administration between 1989 and 2003.[[2]](#cite_note-DFAT-2) President [Bernard Dowiyogo](/wiki/Bernard_Dowiyogo "Bernard Dowiyogo") was first elected in 1976 and served as President till 1978, he returned to that office in 1989, and was re-elected again in 1992.

A vote in parliament, however, forced him to yield power to [Kinza Clodumar](/wiki/Kinza_Clodumar "Kinza Clodumar") in 1995. Dowiyogo regained the presidency when the Clodumar government fell in mid-1998.

In April 2000, [René Harris](/wiki/Ren%C3%A9_Harris "René Harris"), former chairman of the [Nauru Phosphate Corporation](/wiki/Nauru_Phosphate_Corporation "Nauru Phosphate Corporation"), became president as he briefly assembled support in parliament. Harris' attempt to put together an administration lasted for only a few days of parliamentary maneuvering. In the end, Harris proved unable to secure parliament's confidence, and Dowiyogo returned yet again to the presidency by the end of the month, taking office in April 2000 for his fourth and, after a minimal hiatus, fifth stints as Nauru's top executive.

[Bernard Dowiyogo](/wiki/Bernard_Dowiyogo "Bernard Dowiyogo") died in office in March 2003 and [Ludwig Scotty](/wiki/Ludwig_Scotty "Ludwig Scotty") was elected as the president, later being re-elected to serve a full term in October 2004.

Following a [vote of no confidence](/wiki/Motion_of_no_confidence "Motion of no confidence") on 19 December 2007, Scotty was replaced by [Marcus Stephen](/wiki/Marcus_Stephen "Marcus Stephen"). Stephen resigned in November 2011, and [Freddie Pitcher](/wiki/Freddie_Pitcher "Freddie Pitcher") became president. Earth's atmosphere has no definite boundary, gradually becoming thinner and fading into outer space.[[168]](#cite_note-177) Three-quarters of the atmosphere's mass is contained within the first 11 km (6.8 mi) of the surface; this lowest layer is called the troposphere.[[169]](#cite_note-178) Energy from the Sun heats this layer, and the surface below, causing expansion of the air. This lower-density air then rises and is replaced by cooler, higher-density air. The result is [atmospheric circulation](/wiki/Atmospheric_circulation "Atmospheric circulation") that drives the weather and climate through redistribution of thermal energy.[[170]](#cite_note-moran2005-179)

The primary atmospheric circulation bands consist of the [trade winds](/wiki/Trade_winds "Trade winds") in the equatorial region below 30° latitude and the [westerlies](/wiki/Westerlies "Westerlies") in the mid-latitudes between 30° and 60°.[[171]](#cite_note-berger2002-180) [Ocean heat content](/wiki/Ocean_heat_content "Ocean heat content") and [currents](/wiki/Ocean_current "Ocean current") are also important factors in determining climate, particularly the [thermohaline circulation](/wiki/Thermohaline_circulation "Thermohaline circulation") that distributes thermal energy from the equatorial oceans to the polar regions.[[172]](#cite_note-rahmstorf2003-181)

Earth receives 1361 W/m2 of [solar irradiance](/wiki/Solar_irradiance "Solar irradiance").[[3]](#cite_note-earth_fact_sheet-5)[[173]](#cite_note-182) The amount of solar energy that reaches Earth's surface decreases with increasing latitude. At higher latitudes, the sunlight reaches the surface at lower angles, and it must pass through thicker columns of the atmosphere.
